newsitem.title: USA: Motorola falls after Nokia/AT&T deal.
newsitem.headline: Motorola falls after Nokia/AT&T deal.

text.p: Shares of technology giant Motorola Inc fell 1-3/8 to 49-5/8 Thursday after Nokia Oy said it signed a $240 million phone handset contract with AT&T Corp, analysts said.
Under a three-year contract, Finnish telecommunications group Nokia will provide AT&T Wireless Services Inc with handsets using the TDMA (Time Division Multiple Access) technology, Nokia said.
Analysts said Motorola has invested heavily in CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) wireless phone technology, which competes with TDMA.
"This gets back to the war between TDMA and CDMA," said Eric Buck, an analyst for Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. "Motorola has made a bet on CDMA, and they are late getting in."
Nonetheless, some analysts see Motorola taking a cut of the AT&T network in the future.

"Certainly Nokia has inked the deal with AT&T, but I would expect that Motorola would also supply in the future," said Marc Cabi, an analyst for DMG Technology Group. "Motorola has not been as quick, and I think that is reflected."
